title: Reproductive Health
syllabus: Need for reproductive health and prevention of sexually transmitted infections (STIs/STDs); Birth control - Need and Methods, Contraception (Natural, Barrier, IUDs, Oral pills, Injections, Implants, Surgical methods) and Medical Termination of Pregnancy (MTP); Amniocentesis; Infertility and Assisted Reproductive Technologies (ART) – IVF, ET, ZIFT, GIFT, ICSI, IUI.

questions.question: According to the World Health Organisation (WHO), reproductive health means a total well-being in all aspects of reproduction, which includes:
options: Physical, emotional, behavioural, and social aspects
Absence of disease or infirmity only
Normal functioning of reproductive organs only
questions.solution: According to the WHO, reproductive health means a total well-being in all aspects of reproduction, namely physical, emotional, behavioural, and social.

questions.question: India was amongst the first countries in the world to initiate action plans and programmes at a national level to attain total reproductive health as a social goal. These national family planning programmes were initiated in:
questions.solution: India initiated nationwide family planning programmes in 1951. These programmes were periodically improved and expanded under the wider banner of 'Reproductive and Child Health Care (RCH) programmes'.

questions.question: Statutory ban on amniocentesis for sex determination in India was enforced primarily to:
options: Check female foeticide resulting from misuse of the prenatal diagnostic technique
Prevent accidental miscarriages during the procedure
Prevent detection of congenital genetic abnormalities
Encourage IVF and assisted reproduction methods
questions.solution: Amniocentesis is a prenatal diagnostic technique used to detect chromosomal disorders and metabolic defects in a developing fetus. A statutory ban was imposed to legally prevent its misuse for prenatal sex determination leading to female foeticide.

questions.question: 'Saheli', a novel oral contraceptive pill for females developed by scientists at the Central Drug Research Institute (CDRI), Lucknow, is characterized as:
options: A non-steroidal preparation taken 'once-a-week' with very few side effects and high contraceptive value
A daily steroidal combination of estrogen and progesterone
A post-coital emergency pill to be taken within 72 hours
questions.solution: 'Saheli' is an oral contraceptive developed by CDRI, Lucknow. It is a non-steroidal preparation (Ormeloxifene/Centchroman) taken as a 'once-a-week' pill with high contraceptive value and minimal side effects.

questions.question: In the Periodic Abstinence method of natural contraception, couples avoid or abstain from coitus from which days of the menstrual cycle when ovulation could be expected?
options: Day 10 to 17 of the menstrual cycle
Day 1 to 5 of the menstrual cycle
Day 21 to 28 of the menstrual cycle
Day 17 to 25 of the menstrual cycle
questions.solution: In periodic abstinence, couples avoid coitus from day 10 to 17 of the menstrual cycle (the fertile period) when ovulatory chances are maximum, thereby minimizing the chance of fertilization.

questions.question: Lactational amenorrhea (absence of menstruation during intense breastfeeding) serves as a natural contraceptive method based on the principle that:
options: High prolactin levels during intense lactation suppress gonadotropins, preventing ovulation and the cycle
High progesterone destroys sperms entering the vagina
Intense suckling directly blocks the cervix with a mucus plug
Estrogen levels rise sharply, killing the ovum
questions.solution: Lactational amenorrhea is based on the fact that ovulation and the menstrual cycle do not occur during the period of intense lactation following parturition (due to high prolactin suppressing GnRH, LH, and FSH). It is effective up to a maximum period of 6 months postpartum.

questions.question: Which of the following barrier methods of contraception provides the additional, crucial advantage of protecting the user against contracting Sexually Transmitted Infections (STIs) and AIDS?
questions.solution: Condoms are barriers made of thin rubber/latex sheath used to cover the penis or vagina/cervix. Unlike other mechanical barriers (diaphragms, vaults), condoms protect users from contracting STIs and AIDS.

questions.question: Diaphragms, cervical caps, and vaults are reusable rubber barriers inserted into the female reproductive tract. Their contraceptive efficiency is enhanced by using them alongside:
questions.solution: Diaphragms, cervical caps, and vaults are inserted into the female reproductive tract to cover the cervix during coitus. Spermicidal creams, jellies, and foams are usually used along with these barriers to increase their contraceptive efficiency.

questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II regarding the categories of Intrauterine Devices (IUDs) and their examples:

List-I (Category of IUD)List-II (Example)
(A) Non-medicated IUDs(I) Progestasert and LNG-20
(B) Copper-releasing IUDs(II) Lippes loop
(C) Hormone-releasing IUDs(III) CuT, Cu7, and Multiload 375

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution: Non-medicated IUDs: Lippes loop; Copper-releasing IUDs: CuT, Cu7, Multiload 375; Hormone-releasing IUDs: Progestasert, LNG-20.

questions.question: Copper ions released from copper-releasing IUDs (like CuT, Multiload 375) function primarily by:
options: Suppressing sperm motility and reducing the fertilizing capacity of sperms
Making the uterus unsuitable for implantation directly
Preventing the release of ovum from the ovary
questions.solution: Copper ions ($\text{Cu}^{2+}$) released from copper IUDs increase phagocytosis of sperms within the uterus, suppress sperm motility, and diminish the fertilizing capacity of sperms.

questions.question: Hormone-releasing IUDs such as Progestasert and LNG-20 achieve contraception primarily by:
options: Making the uterus unsuitable for implantation and rendering the cervix hostile to sperms
Releasing copper ions that kill sperms instantly
Inducing surgical blockage in the vas deferens
questions.solution: Hormone-releasing IUDs (Progestasert, LNG-20) release small amounts of progestogens that make the uterus unsuitable for implantation and thicken cervical mucus, making the cervix hostile to sperm penetration.

questions.question: Combined oral contraceptive pills containing progestogen or progestogen-estrogen combinations inhibit pregnancy by:
options: Inhibiting ovulation and implantation, as well as altering the quality of cervical mucus to retard sperm entry
Causing permanent phagocytosis of all ova
questions.solution: Oral contraceptive pills contain progestogens or progestogen-estrogen combinations. They work by: (1) inhibiting ovulation via negative feedback on LH/FSH, (2) altering the endometrium to inhibit implantation, and (3) thickening cervical mucus to prevent sperm entry.

questions.question: Administration of progestogens or progestogen-estrogen combinations or IUD insertion within ________ of coitus has been found to be very effective as emergency contraception to avoid pregnancy due to unprotected coitus or rape:
questions.solution: Administration of progestogens or progestogen-estrogen combinations or insertion of an IUD within 72 hours of unprotected sexual intercourse is used as emergency contraception to prevent unwanted pregnancy.

questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II regarding terminal surgical sterilization methods in human males and females:

List-I (Method)List-II (Surgical Procedure & Mechanism)
(A) Vasectomy(I) Small part of fallopian tube is removed or tied up through incision in abdomen or vagina
(B) Tubectomy(II) Small part of vas deferens is removed or tied up through a small incision on the scrotum

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution: Vasectomy: A small part of the vas deferens is cut and tied through a small scrotal incision, preventing sperm transport in semen. Tubectomy: A small part of the fallopian tube is removed or tied up, preventing ovum transport.

questions.question: Surgical sterilization methods (Vasectomy and Tubectomy) are advised as terminal methods for couples, but they have a major limitation because:
options: They interfere with the normal sexual drive (libido)
They stop the production of gametes permanently
questions.solution: Surgical sterilization methods are highly effective with almost zero failure rates, but their reversibility is very poor, which is why they are advised only as terminal methods.

questions.question: Medical Termination of Pregnancy (MTP) or induced abortion was legalized by the Government of India with strict conditions to avoid its misuse in the year:
questions.solution: Government of India legalised Medical Termination of Pregnancy (MTP) in 1971 with strict conditions to prevent misuse (such as illegal sex-selective female foeticide).

questions.question: Nearly how many Medical Terminations of Pregnancy (MTPs) are performed all over the world in a year, accounting for about 1/5th of the total number of conceived pregnancies?
questions.solution: Nearly 45 to 50 million MTPs are performed globally each year, representing approximately one-fifth (20%) of the total number of conceived pregnancies worldwide.

questions.question: Medical Termination of Pregnancy (MTP) is considered relatively much safer during which stage of pregnancy?
options: First trimester (up to 12 weeks of pregnancy)
questions.solution: MTP is considered relatively safe during the first trimester (up to 12 weeks of pregnancy). Second-trimester abortions are much riskier because the fetus becomes intimately associated with maternal tissues.

questions.question: According to the Medical Termination of Pregnancy (Amendment) Act 2017, a pregnancy may be terminated on certain registered medical grounds up to 12 weeks on the opinion of ________, and from 12 to 24 weeks on the opinion of ________:
options: One registered medical practitioner, Two registered medical practitioners
Two registered medical practitioners, One registered medical practitioner
Three registered medical practitioners, Four registered medical practitioners
questions.solution: Under the MTP (Amendment) Act 2017, termination of pregnancy up to 12 weeks requires the opinion of one registered medical practitioner, and from 12 to 24 weeks requires the opinion of two registered medical practitioners.

questions.question: Which of the following sexually transmitted infections (STIs) are completely CURABLE if detected early and treated properly?
options: Hepatitis-B, Genital herpes, and HIV infection
questions.solution: Except for Hepatitis-B, Genital herpes, and HIV infections (which are incurable viral STIs), other bacterial and protozoan STIs like Gonorrhoea, Syphilis, Chlamydiasis, Trichomoniasis, and Genital warts are curable if detected early and treated properly.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a mode of transmission for Hepatitis-B and HIV infections?
options: Sharing food or shaking hands with an infected person
Sharing infected injection needles or surgical instruments
Transfusion of contaminated blood or blood products
From an infected mother to her developing fetus across placenta
questions.solution: Hepatitis-B and HIV are transmitted through sexual contact with infected partners, sharing contaminated injection needles, blood transfusion, and from infected mothers to children. They are not transmitted by casual contact, touching, shaking hands, or sharing food.

questions.question: Pelvic Inflammatory Diseases (PID), ectopic pregnancies, abortions, stillbirths, and infertility are serious long-term complications associated with untreated:
questions.solution: Untreated STIs can lead to complications such as Pelvic Inflammatory Diseases (PID), abortions, stillbirths, ectopic pregnancies, infertility, and even reproductive tract cancers.

questions.question: Individuals in which age group are reported to be highly vulnerable to contracting Sexually Transmitted Infections (STIs)?
questions.solution: According to NCERT, STIs are reported to be very high among individuals in the age group of 15–24 years (the adolescent and young adult demographic).

questions.question: Infertility is defined clinically as the inability of a couple to conceive or produce children despite:
options: 2 years of regular, unprotected sexual cohabitation
questions.solution: Infertility is defined as the inability to conceive or produce children even after 2 years of regular, unprotected sexual cohabitation.

questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II regarding the Assisted Reproductive Technologies (ART):

List-I (Technique)List-II (Procedure / Description)
(A) ZIFT (Zygote Intra Fallopian Transfer)(I) Transfer of an embryo with more than 8 blastomeres into the uterus
(B) IUT (Intra Uterine Transfer)(II) Transfer of a zygote or early embryo up to 8 blastomeres into the fallopian tube
(C) GIFT (Gamete Intra Fallopian Transfer)(III) Transfer of an ovum collected from a donor into the fallopian tube of a female who cannot produce one
(D) ICSI (Intra Cytoplasmic Sperm Injection)(IV) Direct microscopic injection of a single sperm into the cytoplasm of an ovum in the laboratory

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution: ZIFT: Zygote or embryo up to 8 blastomeres transferred into fallopian tube; IUT: Embryo with more than 8 blastomeres transferred into uterus; GIFT: Transfer of donor ovum into the fallopian tube of an infertile woman; ICSI: Sperm is directly injected into the ovum in vitro.

questions.question: In 'Test Tube Baby' programmes, the term In Vitro Fertilization (IVF) refers to:
options: Fertilization occurring outside the body in almost similar conditions as that in the body
Fertilization occurring inside the female reproductive tract directly
Artificial insemination into the uterus without fertilization
Culture of ovarian follicles in liquid nitrogen
questions.solution: In In Vitro Fertilization (IVF), ova from the wife/donor and sperms from the husband/donor are collected and induced to form a zygote under simulated laboratory conditions (outside the body), followed by Embryo Transfer (ET).

questions.question: A woman who cannot produce ova but can provide a suitable internal environment for fertilization and embryonic development is advised to undergo which ART technique?
questions.solution: GIFT (Gamete Intra Fallopian Transfer) involves transfer of an ovum collected from a donor into the fallopian tube of another female who cannot produce one, but can provide a suitable environment for fertilization and development.

questions.question: Infertility cases arising due to inability of the male partner to inseminate the female or due to very low sperm counts (oligozoospermia) in the ejaculate can be corrected by:
options: Administration of non-steroidal estrogen antagonists only
questions.solution: Infertility caused by inability of the male partner to inseminate or very low sperm count can be corrected by Artificial Insemination (AI), where semen collected from the husband or donor is artificially introduced into the vagina or uterus (IUI - Intra-Uterine Insemination).

questions.question:
Read the following statements regarding Contraceptive methods:
Statement I: Intrauterine Devices (IUDs) are one of the most widely accepted methods of contraception in India for females who want to delay pregnancy.
Statement II: IUDs are inserted by the user herself without the assistance of a medical professional.

Choose the correct option:
options: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.solution: Statement I is correct. Statement II is incorrect because IUDs are inserted by doctors or expert nurses through the vagina into the uterus and cannot be inserted by the user herself.

questions.question: Subdermal implants (containing progestogen alone or in combination with estrogen) placed under the skin of females provide effective contraception for:
options: Much longer periods compared to daily oral pills
questions.solution: Subdermal implants (e.g., Norplant) are placed under the skin of the upper arm. Their mode of action is similar to pills, but their effective duration is much longer (up to 3 to 5 years).

questions.question: Which of the following is a non-medicated Intrauterine Device (IUD)?
questions.solution: Lippes loop is a double-S-shaped polyethylene non-medicated IUD that attracts macrophages to promote phagocytosis of sperms in the uterine cavity.

questions.question: Which of the following conditions is an ideal characteristic of a contraceptive method?
options: User-friendly, easily available, effective, reversible with no or least side effects, and non-interfering with sexual drive
Expensive and requiring daily surgical intervention
Suppressing sexual desire and libido completely
questions.solution: An ideal contraceptive should be user-friendly, easily available, effective, and reversible with no or least side-effects, and should not interfere with the sexual drive, desire, or sexual act of the user.

questions.question: In the Coitus Interruptus (withdrawal) method of natural contraception, the male partner withdraws his penis from the vagina:
options: Just before ejaculation, so as to avoid insemination
Immediately after ejaculation inside the vagina
During the first 5 days of the menstrual cycle only
questions.solution: Coitus interruptus or withdrawal is a natural method in which the male partner withdraws his penis from the vagina just before ejaculation, preventing insemination of semen.

questions.question: 'Nirodh' is a popular brand of:
questions.solution: 'Nirodh' is a popular brand of male condoms distributed widely in India through government and commercial channels.

questions.question: Which of the following is an incurable viral sexually transmitted disease?
options: Genital herpes (caused by Herpes Simplex Virus)
questions.solution: Genital herpes (along with HIV and Hepatitis-B) is an incurable viral STI. Gonorrhoea and Syphilis are bacterial, and Trichomoniasis is protozoan, all of which are curable with antibiotics.

questions.question: Amniocentesis is performed by withdrawing a small amount of amniotic fluid surrounding the developing fetus. The fluid contains fetal cells which are analyzed for:
options: Chromosomal abnormalities (e.g., Down's syndrome, Turner's syndrome) and metabolic disorders
questions.solution: Amniocentesis analyzes fetal cells in amniotic fluid to check for chromosomal aberrations (Down's syndrome, Klinefelter's, Turner's) and inborn metabolic errors (e.g., phenylketonuria, sickle-cell anemia) to test for fetal health.

questions.question: A specialized ART laboratory procedure where a single sperm is directly injected into the cytoplasm of an ovum using a microscopic micropipette is:
questions.solution: Intra-Cytoplasmic Sperm Injection (ICSI) is a specialized ART procedure to form an embryo in the laboratory by directly injecting a single sperm into the cytoplasm of an ovum.

questions.question: Why is the second trimester of pregnancy considered dangerous for performing Medical Termination of Pregnancy (MTP)?
options: The fetus becomes intimately connected to maternal uterine tissues via a well-established placenta
MTP drugs are ineffective in the second trimester
The mother's blood volume decreases sharply
Amniotic fluid is completely absent in the second trimester
questions.solution: Second-trimester abortions are much more dangerous because the fetus is larger and intimately connected with the maternal endometrium via the vascular placenta, posing high risks of maternal hemorrhage, uterine perforation, and infection.

questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II regarding the sexually transmitted infections and their causative pathogens:

List-I (STI)List-II (Causative Pathogen)
(A) Syphilis(I) Neisseria gonorrhoeae
(B) Gonorrhoea(II) Treponema pallidum
(C) Genital warts(III) Human Papilloma Virus (HPV)
(D) Trichomoniasis(IV) Trichomonas vaginalis

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution: Syphilis: Treponema pallidum; Gonorrhoea: Neisseria gonorrhoeae; Genital warts: Human Papilloma Virus (HPV); Trichomoniasis: Trichomonas vaginalis (flagellated protozoan).

questions.question: Early symptoms of most Sexually Transmitted Infections (STIs) include:
options: Itching, fluid discharge, slight pain, and swelling in the genital region
High fever, chronic cough, and bone fractures
Immediate kidney failure and yellowing of sclera
Complete loss of memory and paralysis
questions.solution: Early symptoms of STIs are usually localized to the external genitalia and include minor itching, fluid discharge, slight pain, burning micturition, and localized swellings.

questions.question: Oral contraceptive pills ('Pills') must be taken daily for a period of 21 days starting preferably within the first five days of the menstrual cycle, followed by a gap of:
questions.solution: Pills are taken daily for 21 days starting within the first five days of the cycle. After a 7-day pill-free interval (during which withdrawal bleeding/menstruation occurs), the pattern is repeated until contraception is desired.

questions.question: Which of the following statements regarding Vasectomy is INCORRECT?
options: Spermatogenesis is permanently stopped in the testes.
Vasa deferentia are cut and tied.
Erection and normal testosterone production remain unaffected.
questions.solution: In vasectomy, spermatogenesis continues normally in the testes, but the transport of sperms is blocked because the vasa deferentia are severed. The ejaculated semen contains seminal gland fluids without spermatozoa.

questions.question:
Read the following statements:
Statement I: MTP cannot be performed after 20 weeks under any circumstances in India.
Statement II: MTP is used as a regular contraceptive method for family planning.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.solution: Both statements are incorrect. MTP is NOT meant to be used as a routine contraceptive method. Under the MTP (Amendment) Act, termination up to 24 weeks is permissible for special categories of women with medical board approvals, and there is no upper gestational limit if termination is immediately necessary to save the woman's life or for substantial fetal abnormalities.

questions.question: What is the primary mechanism of action of emergency contraceptive pills when taken within 72 hours of unprotected intercourse?
options: Inhibits/delays ovulation and alters the endometrium to prevent fertilization or implantation
Induces immediate delivery of the baby
questions.solution: Emergency contraceptive pills (containing high-dose levonorgestrel) prevent pregnancy by postponing/inhibiting ovulation and preventing implantation if fertilization has already taken place.

questions.question: In In Vitro Fertilization (IVF), when an embryo with MORE than 8 blastomeres is transferred into the uterus, the procedure is termed:
questions.solution: In embryo transfer (ET), the zygote or early embryo (up to 8 blastomeres) is transferred into the fallopian tube (ZIFT), and embryos with more than 8 blastomeres are transferred into the uterus (IUT - Intra Uterine Transfer) to complete further development.
